claims.text: A pre-deposited CrN interlayer can suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature steam exposure.
Adding a CrN interlayer will retain the elemental Cr coating's protective oxidation behavior in normal subcritical water.
The proposed interlayer is located between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The CrN interlayer should be contiguous and nanometer-scale.
CrN has lower diffusivity for Cr atoms than pure Cr.
CrN has lower diffusivity for Zr atoms than pure Cr.
The lower diffusivity of CrN allows it to act as a Cr–Zr diffusion barrier.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will delay premature coating failure at high temperature.
The interlayer will not impede formation of the protective chromium oxide scale in subcritical water.
The modified coating will show reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion relative to the unmodified elemental Cr coating.
The modified coating will show enhanced oxidation resistance relative to the unmodified elemental Cr coating.
The modified coating will have a longer lifetime before coating degradation than the unmodified elemental Cr coating.
The intervention is intended to operate during long-term subcritical-water service at approximately 300 °C.
The intervention is intended to operate during short accident-relevant steam exposure at approximately 1200 °C.
The benefit depends on the CrN interlayer remaining stable during short-term exposure up to approximately 1200 °C.
The benefit depends on the CrN interlayer not impeding protective chromium oxide formation under subcritical-water conditions.
The long-term phase and structural stability of CrN under neutron irradiation and thermal cycling is uncertain.
Performance of the proposed coating architecture on full-size cladding components is uncertain.
